reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
# Box

Box is an AI-powered content management platform founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company describes itself as providing intelligent content management that makes it easy to automate workflows, collaborate internally and externally, and protect sensitive data on one platform. Box serves enterprise customers seeking to access, share, edit, and co-create unstructured content like sales presentations, product specs, and employee handbooks, with the company emphasizing enterprise-grade security and compliance protections including GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA capabilities.

The company's main AI product is Box AI, which lets users harness unstructured data like lease agreements and finance documents to get instant insights and summaries. Box AI integrates with leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for real-time analysis and recommendations. The platform includes workflow automation through a drag-and-drop builder, AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection, and AI-powered e-signature workflows. Box also offers Box AI Studio for developers to customize agents and build AI-powered experiences.

Box is a public company trading under ticker BOX (CIK 0001372612) with reported revenue of $1,177,253,000 for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026. The company maintains presence in multiple MCP server registries, with tools enabling AI agents to access email inboxes, cloud storage, physical mail APIs, and other enterprise data sources. Box has significant law exposure in California, with 220 cases on record in that jurisdiction.
